newsitem.title: USA: Steel of W Va sees Q4 charge, expansion.
newsitem.headline: Steel of W Va sees Q4 charge, expansion.

text.p: Steel of West Virginia Inc said Monday it expects to record a charge of $3,881,000 in the fourth quarter of 1996 as a result of its planned disposal of certain equipment.
The company also said in a release that it was working on a $28 million expansion and modernization program expected to be complete by mid-1998.

President Timothy Duke said in the release that despite the charge to 1996 earnings, the equipment upgrade will provide the company with a "state-of-the-art manufacturing facility" as well as advance production of high quality products on a cost effective basis.

Duke also said that the $28 million expansion and modernization program of the Huntington, W. Va. plant is expected to reduce operating costs and increase rolling capacity by 62 percent to over 420,000 tons per year.
The project, which received approval for phase II, will be funded by a combination of internally generated cash flow and bank debt, the company added.
